verses.text: At that time, Herod the tetrarch heard reports about Jesus.
He told his servants, “This must be John the Baptist raised from the dead. That’s why these powers are working in him.”
Herod had arrested John, tied him up, and put him in prison because of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife.
John had told him, “It isn’t lawful for you to have her.”
Herod wanted to kill John, but he feared the crowds, because they considered John a prophet.
At Herod’s birthday celebration, Herodias’s daughter danced in front of the guests and pleased Herod.
So he swore an oath to give her whatever she asked for.
Prompted by her mother, she said, “Bring me John the Baptist’s head on a platter, right now.”
The king was upset, but because of his oath and the guests at his table, he ordered it to be done.
He sent someone to the prison to behead John.
John’s head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, who took it to her mother.
John’s disciples came, took his body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard the news, he left by boat to a secluded place by himself. The crowds heard and followed him on foot from their towns.
When Jesus came ashore, he saw the large crowd, felt compassion for them, and healed their sick.
That evening, the disciples came to him and said, “This place is deserted, and it’s already late. Send the crowds away so they can go to the villages and buy food for themselves.”
But Jesus told them, “They don’t need to leave. You give them something to eat.”
They said, “All we have here are five loaves of bread and two fish.”
He said, “Bring them here to me.”

He told the crowds to sit on the grass. Then he took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke the loaves, and gave them to the disciples. The disciples handed the food out to the crowds.
Everyone ate and was satisfied. They collected twelve baskets full of the leftover pieces.
About five thousand men ate, not counting the women and children.
Right away, Jesus made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the crowds away.
After sending the crowds away, he went up the mountain by himself to pray. Evening came, and he was there alone.
By then the boat was in the middle of the sea, battered by waves because the wind was against it.
During the fourth watch of the night, Jesus came to them, walking on the sea.
When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they panicked and said, “It’s a ghost!” They cried out in fear.
Jesus spoke to them right away: “Take courage! It’s me. Don’t be afraid.”
Peter answered, “Lord, if it’s really you, tell me to come to you on the water.”
Jesus said, “Come!” Peter got out of the boat and walked on the water toward Jesus.
But when he noticed how strong the wind was, he got scared and began to sink. “Lord, save me!” he shouted.
Jesus immediately reached out, caught him, and said, “You have so little faith. Why did you doubt?”
When they climbed into the boat, the wind stopped.
Those in the boat worshiped him and said, “You really are God’s Son!”
After crossing the sea, they reached the land of Gennesaret.
When the people there recognized Jesus, they sent word throughout the surrounding region. People brought him everyone who was sick,
and they begged him to let them touch even the fringe of his robe. Everyone who touched it was healed.
